Game Instructions

How to Play Buzz City

Buzz City is a three-mini-game city race. Win a mini-game and your side gets to press the losing side’s buzzer once.

The first side to receive 3 buzzer hits loses. The opposing side wins Buzz City.

General Rules

  • Goal: win mini-games so you can press the other side’s buzzer. The first side to receive 3 buzzer hits loses Buzz City.
  • Play format: Buzz City can be played 1 vs 1 or in teams of 2 or 3.
  • Team rotation: in team play, you may appoint which teammate plays each mini-game. Whoever starts a mini-game must finish that mini-game. On the next round / next game, you may tag in a different teammate.
  • No outside help: teammates may encourage each other, but they may not assist in the game itself, give strategic directions during play, touch pieces, or help make moves.
  • General cheating penalty: any cheating, peeking at hidden information, illegal assistance, or breaking a game rule means you must buzz yourself once.

Match Order

  1. Round 1: Crosswalk Dash
  2. Round 2: City Match
  3. Round 3: Tower Stacker
  4. After the first three rounds, the first side to reach 2 buzzer hits chooses the game for Round 4.
  5. If the score reaches 2–2, the other side chooses the game for the fifth and final round.
1. Crosswalk Dash

Race your token along the 20-space crosswalk. You must land exactly on space 20 to win. If a roll takes you beyond 20, you bust and return to Start.

Use more dice while you are far from the finish and reduce the number as you get closer. When you are 6 spaces or fewer from 20, roll 1 die.

Roll → Move → Pick Up. After rolling, you must move your token the full rolled amount before you may pick up your die / dice and roll again.

If you reroll early, skip movement, move the wrong amount, or otherwise break the movement sequence, the general cheating penalty applies: buzz yourself once.

2. City Match
Setup
  1. At station two there is one stacked, shuffled deck face-down.
  2. You may pick up the deck and shuffle it as much as you want, but you may not look at your cards while they are in your hand / deck.
Dealing & Matching Phase
  1. When ready, reveal the top card from the deck, then reveal the next top card.
  2. If those two newly revealed cards match each other, place them together in a matched pile, face-up.
  3. If those two newly revealed cards do not match, turn them face-down in the play area.
  4. Go back to the deck. You may shuffle again, but you still may not look at your cards in hand.
  5. Reveal the next top card from the deck.
  6. If this new revealed card matches a previously dealt face-down card and you remember where that match is, you may flip that remembered face-down card. If they match, place the pair in your matched pile and return to the deck.
  7. If you attempt that remembered match and you are wrong, turn both cards face-down in the play area.
  8. If your newly revealed first card does not match a previously dealt face-down card, reveal a second new card from the top of the deck.
  9. If the first and second new cards match each other, place them together in your matched pile.
  10. If they do not match each other, turn both face-down in the play area.
  11. Important restriction: if your second new card happens to match a previously dealt face-down card that you remember, you still may not use that remembered match right then. Because it is your second new card, it may only try to match the first new card. If the two new cards do not match each other, both must be turned face-down, and you must wait until a later turn to use that remembered match.
  12. Continue this process until all cards from the deck have been dealt, making matches along the way whenever allowed above.
Standard Match Pair Phase
  1. Once your deck has been fully dealt, continue with the remaining face-down cards using a normal memory-match mechanic.
  2. Flip two face-down cards per attempt. A match is claimed; a miss is turned back face-down.
  3. The first player or team to match all of their pairs wins City Match.
3. Tower Stacker

Use the building-decal cards to build a fast house-of-cards tower.

Build two leaning 2-card triangles on the bottom. Lay one bridge card across those two lower supports. Then build one more leaning 2-card triangle on top of the bridge.

Bottom: 2-card triangle + 2-card triangle • Middle: 1 bridge card • Top: 2-card triangle

The tower must stand on its own. If it collapses before completion, rebuild. The first side to complete the stable structure wins.

Buzzer Rule

After every mini-game, the winner presses the losing side’s buzzer once. The app tracks buzzer hits automatically. When a side reaches 3 hits, that side loses Buzz City.

Individual Buzzer

Use Individual Buzzer as a standalone counter. Set the target number of hits and press the buzzer until the target is reached. It saves separately from team play.
